item.title: Iran officials say will not negotiate with US — Bloomberg
item.description: Iran’s national security chief, Ali Larijani, said the country will not negotiate with the United States in response to reports that he reached out to Washington via Oman mediators, Bloomberg reported on Monday.

item.title: WTI Price Forecast: Retreats from seven-month top, still well bid near $71.00 mark
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Crude Oil prices trim a part of strong intraday gains to levels beyond the $73.00 mark, or the highest since June 2025, touched this Monday in reaction to a dramatic escalation of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Pound Sterling declines against its peers amid Middle East tensions
item.description: The Pound Sterling underperforms its major currency pairs, except antipodeans, and is down 0.6% to near 1.3400 against the US Dollar (USD) during the late Asian trading session on Monday.

item.title: BoJ’s Himino says could raise rates toward neutral if underlying inflation accelerates to target
item.description: Bank of Japan (BoJ) Deputy Governor Himino said on Monday that even if headline inflation falls below 2%, the central bank could raise interest rates toward neutral if it judge underlying inflation is accelerating to our price target.

item.title: USD/CAD holds gains above 1.3650 ahead of ISM Manufacturing PMI
item.description: USD/CAD gains ground after registering modest losses in the previous session, trading around 1.3660 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) rises on increased safe-haven demand amid escalating Middle East tensions.

item.title: Brent: War-driven spike tests risk appetite – UOB
item.description: UOB Global Economics & Markets Research highlights a sharp jump in Brent crude after US-Israel strikes on Iran and an OPEC+ decision to raise output.

item.title: EUR/USD: Oil shock risk supports Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen argues that escalating conflict in the Middle East and a potential Oil supply shock are negative for EUR/USD. The bank highlights the United States’ reserve currency role, its net Oil exporter status and relatively stronger economic resilience versus the Euro area.

item.title: USD/CHF gains to near 0.7700 as US Dollar firms, US Manufacturing PMI data in focus
item.description: The USD/CHF pair gathers strength to around 0.7695 during the early European trading hours on Monday.
